contribution: Contribution 2 — PillarJEPA trains stably (real gradient-descent loop)
gap_closed: PillarJEPA.onUpdate() and JEPAObjective.onUpdate() are both EMPTY ("weight updates expected externally"). No loop ever updated the predictor weights; reported numbers were deterministic-init baseline. This experiment supplies the missing external gradient-descent loop and measures whether the REAL assembled objective is trainable.
real_components_used: packages/core/src/traits/JEPAPredictor.ts :: JEPAPredictor (forward/getWeights/setWeights — the actual MLP, unmodified)
packages/core/src/traits/pillar/PillarJEPA.ts :: pillarJepaHandler (driven for cross-check of assembled L_total)

method.gradients: EXACT analytic backprop through the real MLP (dL/dẑ closed-form for MSE+SIGReg+conservation; conservation hinge is the IMPORTED function). NOT finite-difference, NOT autodiff dependency.
method.data: conservation-respecting synthetic transitions: target lies near axisIdToDirection("energy") with conserved magnitude ∈[0.85,1.0] + small Gaussian noise.
method.temporal_gating: κ rises 0→1 over training; λ_c_eff = λ_c·(1−κ).
method.handler_crosscheck: real pillarJepaHandler driven with synced weights; jepaTotalLoss compared to ours. NOTE: the handler uses its OWN context encoder (EmbeddingTrait deterministic hash of a string), so its MSE term differs from our structured-context MSE by construction — the reported max_handler_delta is that expected gap, not an error.
